docs.title: Git Maestro
docs.text: A convenient TUI for managing git repositories with interactive menus

docs.title: What is Git Maestro?
docs.text: Git Maestro is a context-aware command-line interface that streamlines your git workflow by observing your repository state and presenting intelligent, actionable options. No more typing countless git commands or constantly switching to your browser—just select from a beautiful interactive menu and let Git Maestro handle the rest.

docs.title: What Problem Does It Solve?
docs.text:
Modern software development involves juggling multiple tasks: - Setting up new repositories with proper configuration - Managing remotes across GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps - Monitoring CI/CD pipelines and debugging failures - Keeping repositories clean and organized

Git Maestro eliminates this friction by: - Detecting your current context and showing only relevant actions - Automating repetitive tasks like creating READMEs, .gitignore files, and remote repositories - Providing AI integration through Model Context Protocol (MCP) for autonomous workflow automation - Offering a beautiful CLI experience with rich formatting and interactive prompts

docs.title: Who Is It For?
docs.text:
Git Maestro is designed for:

  • Developers who want to streamline their git workflow
  • DevOps engineers managing multiple repositories
  • AI assistants (via MCP) that need to autonomously manage git operations and monitor CI/CD
  • Teams looking for consistent repository setup and management

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Context-Aware Actions: Only shows actions relevant to your current repository state
  • Beautiful CLI Interface: Built with Rich and Prompt Toolkit for a polished experience
  • Modular Design: Easy to extend with custom actions
  • Fast Setup: Quickly initialize repos, add READMEs, .gitignore files, and remotes
  • Git Plugin Support: Can be called as git maestro after installation
  • MCP Integration: Seamlessly works with Model Context Protocol for AI-powered workflows

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Install Git Maestro with pip:

pip install git-maestro

Then run it in any directory:

git-maestro

Or use it as a git plugin:

git maestro

docs.title: Token Storage
docs.text:
Git Maestro stores authentication tokens securely in your home directory:

~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf

This file is automatically created when you first authenticate with GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps.

Important: This file is outside your repository and should never be committed to version control.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Git Maestro supports the following environment variables:

docs.title: GitHub Token
docs.text:
Environment variable: GITHUB_TOKEN

If set, Git Maestro will use this token for GitHub API authentication instead of prompting you.

export GITHUB_TOKEN="<your-github-token>"
git-maestro

docs.title: GitLab Token
docs.text:
Environment variable: GITLAB_TOKEN

If set, Git Maestro will use this token for GitLab API authentication.

export GITLAB_TOKEN="<your-gitlab-token>"
git-maestro

docs.title: Azure DevOps Token
docs.text:
Environment variable: AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT

If set, Git Maestro will use this token for Azure DevOps API authentication.

export AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT="<your-azure-token>"
git-maestro

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
Currently, Git Maestro stores minimal configuration:

  • Token storage: ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf

Future versions may add support for: - Default repository visibility (public/private) - Preferred remote provider - Custom action configurations

docs.title: MCP Server Configuration
docs.text:
To use Git Maestro as an MCP server with Claude Code, add this to your mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "git-maestro": {
      "command": "git-maestro",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Or with a custom Python environment:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "git-maestro": {
      "command": "/path/to/your/venv/bin/git-maestro",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Token Management
docs.text:
1. Never commit tokens to version control
  2. Rotate tokens regularly (every 90 days recommended)
  3. Use fine-grained tokens when available
  4. Revoke unused tokens immediately
  5. Store tokens securely (use environment variables or secure config files)

docs.title: Repository Security
docs.text: Git Maestro's default .gitignore templates block common sensitive files: - *.token - .env - credentials.json - secrets.* - ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Ensure your token storage directory has restrictive permissions:

chmod 700 ~/.config/git-maestro
chmod 600 ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf

docs.title: Token Not Saved
docs.text:
If Git Maestro keeps prompting for your token:

  1. Check that ~/.config/git-maestro/ exists and is writable
  2. Verify file permissions allow writing
  3. Check for errors in the console output

docs.title: API Rate Limiting
docs.text:
If you hit GitHub's rate limit:

  1. Verify you're using an authenticated token
  2. Check your rate limit status: curl -H "Authorization: token YOUR_TOKEN" https://api.github.com/rate_limit
  3. Wait for the limit to reset (shown in the response)

docs.title: MCP Server Not Connecting
docs.text:
If Claude Code can't connect to the MCP server:

  1. Verify git-maestro mcp runs successfully in your terminal
  2. Check that the path in mcp.json is correct
  3. Ensure Git Maestro is installed in the environment Claude Code is using

docs.title: GitHub API Integration
docs.text: Git Maestro integrates with GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps APIs to automate repository management and CI/CD monitoring.

docs.title: Required Scopes
docs.text:
To create repositories and access GitHub Actions data, Git Maestro requires a Personal Access Token (PAT) with these scopes:

  • repo - Full control of private repositories (includes public repos)
  • workflow - Update GitHub Action workflows (for accessing Actions data)

docs.title: Creating a GitHub Personal Access Token
docs.text:
1. Go to GitHub Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic)
  2. Click Generate new token (classic)
  3. Give it a descriptive name like "Git Maestro"
  4. Select the following scopes:
  5. repo (all sub-scopes)
  6. workflow
  7. Click Generate token
  8. Copy the token immediately (you won't see it again)

docs.title: Authentication Method
docs.text:
Git Maestro uses Personal Access Token (PAT) authentication:

# Git Maestro will prompt for your token when needed
git-maestro

Your token is stored securely in ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf and never committed to any repository.

docs.title: Available GitHub Operations
docs.text:
• Create Repository: Create a new GitHub repository (public or private)
  • List Workflow Runs: Get recent GitHub Actions runs
  • Get Job Details: View job structure and status for a workflow run
  • Check Job Status: Lightweight polling for CI/CD status
  • Download Logs: Fetch logs for specific jobs or all failed jobs

docs.title: Required Scopes
docs.text:
For GitLab, you need a Personal Access Token with:

  • api - Full API access

docs.title: Creating a GitLab Personal Access Token
docs.text:
1. Go to GitLab Settings → Access Tokens
  2. Enter a name like "Git Maestro"
  3. Select scope: api
  4. Click Create personal access token
  5. Copy the token immediately

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: Git Maestro will prompt for your GitLab token when you select GitLab as your remote provider.

docs.title: Required Access
docs.text:
For Azure DevOps, you need a Personal Access Token with:

  • Code - Read & Write
  • Build - Read & Execute

docs.title: Creating an Azure DevOps Personal Access Token
docs.text:
1. Go to Azure DevOps → User Settings → Personal Access Tokens
  2. Click New Token
  3. Select scopes:
  4. Code: Read & Write
  5. Build: Read & Execute
  6. Click Create
  7. Copy the token immediately

docs.title: MCP Tools for GitHub Actions
docs.text: When running as an MCP server, Git Maestro exposes these tools for AI assistants:

docs.title: list_github_actions_runs(count)
docs.text:
Get the most recent workflow runs.

Parameters: - count (optional, default: 10) - Number of runs to retrieve

Returns: List of workflow runs with status, conclusion, and metadata

docs.title: get_github_actions_run_jobs(run_id)
docs.text:
View job structure and details for a specific workflow run.

Parameters: - run_id (required) - The workflow run ID

Returns: List of jobs with names, statuses, conclusions, and steps

docs.title: check_github_actions_job_status(run_id, job_id)
docs.text:
Lightweight status check (fast polling without downloading logs).

Parameters: - run_id (required) - The workflow run ID - job_id (optional) - Specific job ID to check

Returns: Status summary (queued, in_progress, completed)

docs.title: download_github_actions_job_logs(run_id, job_id)
docs.text:
Fetch logs for a specific job.

Parameters: - run_id (required) - The workflow run ID - job_id (required) - The job ID

Returns: Full job logs as text

docs.title: download_job_traces()
docs.text:
Download all failed job logs from the latest workflow run.

Returns: Combined logs from all failed jobs

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
GitHub API has rate limits: - Authenticated requests: 5,000 requests/hour - Unauthenticated requests: 60 requests/hour

Git Maestro uses authenticated requests for all API calls to maximize your rate limit.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
• Store tokens in ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf (outside repositories)
  • Never commit tokens to version control
  • Use fine-grained tokens when possible
  • Rotate tokens regularly
  • Revoke tokens you no longer use

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.9
  • Git installed on your system

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
The easiest way to install Git Maestro is via pip:

pip install git-maestro

This will install the git-maestro command globally, making it available from any directory.

docs.title: Install as Git Plugin
docs.text:
After installation, Git Maestro can be used as a git plugin:

git maestro

This works automatically because git looks for executables named git-* in your PATH.

docs.title: Development Installation
docs.text: If you want to contribute to Git Maestro or modify it for your needs:

docs.title: Using PDM (Recommended)
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/benhuckvale/git-maestro.git
cd git-maestro

# Install dependencies with PDM
pdm install

# Run in development mode
pdm run git-maestro

docs.title: Using pip
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/benhuckvale/git-maestro.git
cd git-maestro

# Install in editable mode
pip install -e .

# Run from anywhere
git-maestro

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
After installation, verify it works:

git-maestro --help

You should see the help message with available commands and options.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Git Maestro automatically installs these dependencies:

  • rich>=13.7.0 - Terminal formatting and styling
  • prompt-toolkit>=3.0.43 - Interactive prompts
  • gitpython>=3.1.40 - Git repository interaction
  • PyGithub>=2.1.1 - GitHub API integration
  • python-gitlab>=4.4.0 - GitLab API integration
  • azure-devops>=7.1.0b4 - Azure DevOps API integration

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Git Maestro is designed with privacy in mind. This document explains what data is accessed, what is stored, and what is never persisted.

docs.title: What Data Is Accessed
docs.text: Git Maestro accesses the following data to function:

docs.title: Local Repository Data
docs.text:
• Git repository status and configuration
  • Local branch information
  • Remote URLs and configurations
  • File listings (to detect README, .gitignore, etc.)

docs.title: Remote API Data (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps)
docs.text: When you use remote repository features, Git Maestro accesses: - Your repository list - Repository metadata (name, visibility, URL) - GitHub Actions workflow runs and job statuses - Job logs for CI/CD monitoring

docs.title: Authentication Tokens
docs.text:
• Personal Access Tokens (PATs) for GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps
  • Tokens are stored locally only (see below)

docs.title: What Data Is Stored
docs.text: Git Maestro stores minimal data on your local system:

docs.title: Authentication Tokens
docs.text:
Location: ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf

This file contains your API tokens for GitHub, GitLab, and Azure DevOps.

Security measures: - Stored outside your repository (never committed) - File permissions should be 600 (read/write for owner only) - Tokens are stored in plain text locally (you are responsible for filesystem security)

docs.title: No Other Persistent Storage
docs.text: Git Maestro does not store: - Repository data - Workflow logs - User preferences - Usage analytics - Telemetry data

docs.title: What Data Is Never Persisted
docs.text:
The following data is only used in memory during execution and never written to disk:

  • Repository file contents
  • Git commit history
  • Workflow run details
  • Job logs (unless you explicitly save them)
  • API responses

docs.title: API Calls
docs.text:
Git Maestro makes direct API calls to: - api.github.com (GitHub) - gitlab.com or your GitLab instance (GitLab) - dev.azure.com (Azure DevOps)

All API calls use HTTPS for encryption in transit.

docs.title: No Third-Party Analytics
docs.text: Git Maestro does not: - Send telemetry to any third party - Track usage statistics - Report errors to external services - Phone home for updates

docs.title: MCP Server Privacy
docs.text:
When running as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, Git Maestro:

  • Exposes tools to the connected AI assistant (e.g., Claude Code)
  • All data accessed through MCP tools follows the same privacy rules above
  • The AI assistant may see repository data and logs you explicitly request
  • No data is sent to third parties beyond the AI service you're using

docs.title: Your Responsibility
docs.text:
• Protect your ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf file
  • Use filesystem permissions to restrict access
  • Rotate tokens regularly
  • Revoke tokens when no longer needed

docs.title: Our Commitment
docs.text:
• We never transmit your tokens to any server except the API they're intended for
  • Tokens are never logged or included in error messages
  • We use tokens only for authenticated API calls you initiate

docs.title: GitHub Developer Program Compliance
docs.text:
Git Maestro is suitable for the GitHub Developer Program because:

  1. Transparent API usage: All API calls are documented and user-initiated
  2. Secure token handling: Tokens are stored locally and never shared
  3. No data harvesting: We don't collect or store user data beyond what's necessary
  4. Clear privacy policy: This document explains all data access and storage
  5. Open source: All code is available for review

docs.title: Data Deletion
docs.text:
To remove all data stored by Git Maestro:

rm -rf ~/.config/git-maestro

This deletes all stored tokens. You can then revoke the tokens from: - GitHub Personal Access Tokens - GitLab Access Tokens - Azure DevOps Personal Access Tokens

docs.title: Changes to This Policy
docs.text: This privacy policy may be updated as Git Maestro evolves. Check the repository for the latest version.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text: For privacy concerns or questions, please open an issue on the GitHub repository.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Accessed: Local git data, remote API data (when you request it), your API tokens

Stored: API tokens only (in ~/.config/git-maestro/tokens.conf)

Never Persisted: Repository contents, logs, workflow data, analytics, telemetry

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Navigate to any directory and run:

git-maestro

Or use it as a git plugin:

git maestro

docs.title: What Happens Next?
docs.text:
Git Maestro will:

  1. Detect the current state of your directory
  2. Show you what's configured and what's missing
  3. Present a menu of applicable actions
  4. Execute your selected action
  5. Refresh and show updated options

docs.title: Example: Setting Up a New Project
Step 1: Initialize a Git Repository
docs.text:
Start in an empty directory:

mkdir my-new-project
cd my-new-project
git-maestro

You'll see an option to Initialize Git Repository. Select it, and Git Maestro will run git init.

docs.title: Step 2: Add a README
docs.text: After initialization, Git Maestro shows new options. Select Add README.md to create a basic README template.

docs.title: Step 3: Add a .gitignore
docs.text: Select Add .gitignore and choose a template (Python, Node.js, or Generic).

docs.title: Step 4: Setup Remote Repository
docs.text:
Select Setup Remote Repository and choose your platform (GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps). Git Maestro will:

  • Prompt you for authentication if needed
  • Create the remote repository
  • Add it as your origin
  • Push your initial commit

docs.title: Example: Using MCP for AI-Powered Workflows
docs.text: Git Maestro includes an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that enables AI assistants to autonomously manage your repository and monitor CI/CD.

docs.title: Start the MCP Server
docs.text: git-maestro mcp

docs.title: Configure Claude Code
docs.text:
Add to your mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "git-maestro": {
      "command": "git-maestro",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: AI-Powered Workflow Example
docs.text:
Once configured, an AI assistant can:

  1. Make code changes and push them
  2. Monitor GitHub Actions with check_github_actions_job_status()
  3. Download failing job logs with download_github_actions_job_logs()
  4. Analyze failures and apply fixes
  5. Repeat until all tests pass

This creates a fully autonomous development loop.

docs.title: Available Actions
docs.text:
Git Maestro provides these context-aware actions:

  • Initialize Git Repository - Run git init in non-git directories
  • Add README.md - Create a README with basic project structure
  • Add .gitignore - Add a .gitignore file (Python, Node.js, or Generic templates)
  • Setup Remote Repository - Configure GitHub, GitLab, or Azure DevOps as remote origin

More actions are being added regularly!
